restatement: Values reach the template resolver from n8n as strings. The card fixes two defects in how those strings are coerced. First, repairing a JSON object or array string must remove only structural commas (leading, trailing, doubled) and must never rewrite commas inside string literals. Second, a numeric path segment on a string input (tags.0) must index through the same array coercion FOR uses, so that both 'a,b' and '["a","b"]' index like arrays, in ${{...}} output and in IF conditions. The change must not alter any other behavior, edit existing tests or add a runtime dependency. It serves a cycle goal of fixing the Tier 0 bugs while keeping the core pure and CI green.
verification_plan: c1: trace '{"name":"a,, b"}', '{"name":"x,}"}', '{"a":"{,x","b":"[,y","c":"z,]"}' and '{"name":"a,, b",}' through object repair and confirm that string contents come out byte-identical and the structural trailing comma is still removed
c2: trace '["a, b","c,]d"]' and '["[,x","y,,z"]' through array coercion as FOR uses it and confirm each element is preserved exactly
c3: trace ${{tags.0}}/${{tags.1}} and IF tags.0 == "a" with tags='a,b' through both the interpreter lookup and the expressions resolveValue lookup
c4: trace the same with tags='["a","b"]' in output and in IF conditions
For each frozen test, decide whether it failed before the change for the stated reason and passes after it. The guard tests must pass both before and after.

m1: list every input whose result changes besides the named defects: escaped quotes in strings, whitespace around commas, comma runs in the middle of an array, non-numeric segments on array strings in conditions, plain non-JSON strings indexed by a number
m2: confirm the diff touches no test file
m3: confirm no package.json or dependency change and no new import outside sibling modules
Scope: confirm only coercion.ts, expressions.ts and interpreter.ts change

findings.title: Conditions lose non-numeric property access on JSON-array strings (for example tags.length), a behavior change outside the named defects

serves.scenario: Before the change, expressions.resolveValue ran JSON.parse on any string intermediate, so with tags='["a","b"]' a condition such as {{IF tags.length > 1}} reached the parsed array and could read its 'length' property. After the change, tryCoerceStringForPathSegment returns null for a non-numeric segment on a string that is not an object, so resolveValue returns null. The ordering comparison then throws TypeError, or == yields a different result. No defect named in the card asks for this change.

findings.rubric: no change outside the card scope / must not change behavior outside the named defects
findings.reproduction: With base e7069db and head 2a63dc1, run resolveTemplate('{{IF tags.length > 1}}Y{{ELSE}}N{{END_IF}}', new Map([['tags','["a","b"]']]), {strictMode:false}). This holds if the lookup code after the string branch in resolveValue resolves own or array properties such as 'length', which is plausible because it previously received the JSON.parse result unchanged. Expect 'Y' at base and a thrown TypeError, or 'N', at head. The smallest fix: in resolveValue, keep the old JSON.parse result as a fallback when tryCoerceStringForPathSegment returns null, or apply the array coercion only for numeric segments and otherwise keep the JSON.parse behavior.

findings.title: Conditions now repair malformed object strings, and array repair now also collapses comma runs in the middle of an array and commas after '{'

serves.scenario: In IF conditions, '{"a":1,}' used to fail JSON.parse and give null; it now repairs and resolves. In tryCoerceToArray, '["a",,"b"]' used to fail JSON.parse and fall back to comma splitting; it now parses as ["a","b"]. Both changes follow the card's goal that one coercion serves everywhere and that only structural commas are repaired, so neither needs a fix. They are behavior changes the lead may want recorded.

findings.rubric: no change outside the card scope
findings.reproduction: Run {{IF o.a == 1}}Y{{ELSE}}N{{END_IF}} with o='{"a":1,}' (base: N, head: Y). Run {{FOR a AS x}}[${{x}}]{{END_FOR}} with a='["a",,"b"]' and compare base with head.
